rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah presents worship of God, the religion of tawhid, as the path of prophetic felicity; abandoning their way through neglect of prayer and desire is error, except for repentant believers who act righteously.
rows.anchor: الذي يستفاد من سياقها بيان أن عبادته تعالى - وهو دين التوحيد - هو دين أهل السعادة والرشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 58–60, especially their opening verses, state the surah’s central purpose as an inference from the stories; this mid-surah statement distinguishes it from long surahs that signal aims only at openings and endings.
rows.anchor: الآيات وخاصة الثلاث الأول منها تتضمن حاق غرض السورة وقد أوردته في صورة الاستنباط من القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative points to the named figures in the preceding stories; those stories exemplify the blessed, and this verse and the next two are their inferred conclusion.
rows.anchor: إلى المذكورين قبل الآية في السورة وهم زكريا ويحيى ومريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Read those blessed as an adjective of the demonstrative and the recitation clause as its predicate; making the blessed clause the predicate and recitation a second predicate fits the surah’s purpose less well.
rows.anchor: مشيرا إلى أصحاب القصص بأعيانهم مبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s unrestricted statement that He bestowed grace means these people received divine favor without punishment; felicity is precisely grace untroubled by punishment.
rows.anchor: أنعم عليهم وأطلق القول فيهم ففيه دلالة على أنهم قد غشيتهم النعمة الإلهية من غير نقمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed are people of the straight path, protected from wrath and error and secure in guidance; the linked verse says believers who do not mix faith with wrongdoing have safety and guidance.
rows.anchor: أصحاب الصراط المستقيم المصونون عن الغضب والضلال ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم في أمن من كل خطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition min in from among the prophets is partitive and parallels from among those We guided and chose.
rows.anchor: من فيه للتبعيض وعديله قوله الآتي

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes take min as explanatory, but this does not fit the demonstrative’s reference to previously named individuals because prophets are a broader class.
rows.anchor: وقد جوز المفسرون كون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanatory reading can be maintained only if the named figures are examples of the blessed, so that the meaning includes them and their prophetic and guided peers.
rows.anchor: إلا أن يكون إشارة إليهم بما هم أمثلة لأهل السعادة ويكون المعنى أولئك المذكورون وأمثالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From Adam’s descendants qualifies the prophets and is partitive, meaning prophets who are some of Adam’s descendants; it cannot explain the prophets without distorting the meaning.
rows.anchor: في معنى الصفة للنبيين ومن فيه للتبعيض أي من النبيين الذين هم بعض ذرية آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those carried with Noah are the ark’s passengers and their descendants, whom God blessed; they are Noah’s descendants, as the cited verse states.
rows.anchor: المراد بهم المحمولون في سفينة نوح عليه السلام وذريتهم وقد بارك الله عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse divides the blessed prophets into four lineage groups; although later lineages are included in earlier ones, the enumeration signals successive waves of prophetic grace and felicity for humanity.
rows.anchor: وقد قسم الله تعالى الذين أنعم عليهم من النبيين على هذه الطوائف الأربع أعني ذرية آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier stories supply examples from each lineage: Idris from Adam, Abraham from Noah’s descendants, Isaac and Jacob from Abraham, and the listed later figures from Israel.
rows.anchor: من كل من الذراري الأربع كإدريس من ذرية آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those guided and chosen are another class of recipients of grace besides prophets, since divine favor is not restricted to prophethood.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء غير النبيين من الذين أنعم الله عليهم فإن هذه النعمة غير خاصة بالنبيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary is not a prophet, so those guided and chosen include nonprophetic truthful people, martyrs, and righteous; Mary herself is among the truthful.
rows.anchor: وليست من النبيين فالمراد بقوله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: The view that the guided-and-chosen clause coordinates with from among the prophets while min is explanatory conflicts with the contextual reading; apparent grammatical difference need not mean different referents, only a distinction in description.
rows.anchor: يظهر فساد قول من جعل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: The alternative coordination with from Adam’s descendants, taking min as partitive, is likewise unsound under the preceding contextual analysis.
rows.anchor: ونظيره قول من قال بكونه معطوفا على قوله

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim treats the guided-and-chosen phrase as an independent sentence with an omitted subject; the author rejects this unsupported ellipsis because it breaks the passage’s contrast between righteous predecessors, bad successors, and repentant returners.
rows.anchor: والوجه منسوب إلى أبي مسلم المفسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about recitation is the predicate of the blessed group; detaching the guided-and-chosen phrase as a new sentence destroys the surah’s purpose of describing their reverence before contrasting their successors.
rows.anchor: الغرض منها بيان طريقة أولئك العباد المنعم عليهم وأنهم كانوا خاضعين لله خاشعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sujjadan is the plural of prostrating worshipper and bukiyyan is a fuʿul plural of weeping person; falling prostrate and weeping may figuratively express complete submission and humility.
rows.anchor: السجد جمع ساجد والبكي على فعول جمع باكي والجملة خبر للذين في صدر الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the figurative reading, the verses are any mention of divine matters being recited, and the group responds with complete reverence and humility.
rows.anchor: الخرور سجدا وبكيا كناية عن كمال الخضوع والخشوع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The author rejects restricting the recitation to all scripture or scripture about punishment, sujud to ritual prayer or prostration of recitation, and weeping to the moment of hearing or reciting.
rows.anchor: إن المراد بتلاوة الآيات قراءة الكتب السماوية مطلقا أو خصوص ما يشتمل على عذاب الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed, among them prophets and other guided people, humble themselves before the Merciful when He is mentioned and His signs are recited.
rows.anchor: خاضعون للرحمن خاشعون إذا ذكر عندهم وتليت آياته عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording does not say they used to respond this way in the past, because the focus is the types of people—righteous predecessors, corrupt successors, and repentant returners—without a temporal restriction.
rows.anchor: لأن العناية في المقام متعلقة ببيان حال النوع من غير نظر إلى ماضي الزمان ومستقبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The corrupt successors replaced the earlier people of worshipful submission but treated inherited prayer and devotion carelessly, turning away from God and pursuing desires that distract from striving for Him.
rows.anchor: قام مقام أولئك الذين أنعم الله عليهم وكانت طريقتهم الخضوع والخشوع لله تعالى بالتوجه إليه بالعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasting prayer means corrupting it through neglect and contempt, even altering or playing with it and eventually abandoning it after acceptance; it does not mean simply never undertaking it.
rows.anchor: المراد بإضاعة الصلاة افسادها بالتهاون فيها والاستهانة بها حتى ينتهي إلى أمثال اللعب بها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The author rejects the gloss that wasting prayer simply means leaving it altogether, since one cannot waste what one never took up or received.
rows.anchor: فما قيل أن المراد بإضاعه الصلاة تركها ليس بسديد إذ لا يسمى ترك الشيء من رأس إضاعة له

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Ghayy may mean the recompense for their error, comparable to the punishment called atham elsewhere.
rows.anchor: أي جزاء غيهم على ما قيل فهو كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ghayy is the error itself as the destination of their path: it will be exposed at resurrection or become rooted in their hearts, making them allies of Satan.
rows.anchor: ومن الممكن أن يكون المراد به نفس الغي بفرض الغي غاية للطريق التي يسلكونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the latter reading the expression is a subtle metaphor by implicit comparison: those following this path eventually reach its destination of error.
rows.anchor: وكيف كان فهو استعارة بالكناية لطيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage says the repentant receive the promised reward in full, so the denial of injustice follows from complete recompense.
rows.anchor: فإنه من لوازم توفية الأجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entering Paradise names the result in place of its cause; the underlying promise is that their reward will be paid in full, as the following denial of injustice confirms.
rows.anchor: من وضع المسبب موضع السبب والأصل فأولئك يوفون أجرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAdn means abiding, so the name of these gardens points to the permanence of their inhabitants’ stay.
rows.anchor: العدن الإقامة ففي تسميتها به إشارة إلى خلودها لداخليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A promise made in the unseen concerns what the recipient cannot perceive; a promise that is coming cannot fail.
rows.anchor: الوعد بالغيب هو الوعد بما ليس تحت إدراك الموعود له

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ explains the active sense of the passive participle by saying that what a person comes to has come to that person; it also reports that the promised garden is what believers come to.
rows.anchor: قال في المجمع والمفعول هنا بمعنى الفاعل لأن ما أتيته فقد أتاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The absence of idle talk is a distinctive feature of Paradise; سلام is an independent exception and means that everything encountered there is harmless, unlike merely being safe from a speaker’s harm.
rows.anchor: واستثناء السلام منه استثناء منفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greetings of peace in Paradise come from angels and the inhabitants’ companions.
rows.anchor: وإنما يسمعون السلام من الملائكة ومن رفقائهم في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their provision arriving morning and evening is a figure for its uninterrupted succession.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن إتيان الرزق بكرة وعشيا كناية عن تواليه من غير انقطاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise is called an inheritance because it was promised broadly to people of faith and good works, while the pious receive it exclusively after others are deprived through neglect and desire.
rows.anchor: اختصاص المتقين بها بعد حرمان غيرهم عنها بإضاعه الصلاة واتباع الشهوات وراثة المتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden is promised conditionally on faith and righteous action, so the pious receive it as an earned reward.
rows.anchor: الوعد الإلهي المشروط بالإيمان والعمل الصالح

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: A report in al-Majmaʿ from ʿAli ibn al-Husayn says that the guided-and-chosen people are the Imams’ family; al-Tabatabaʾi accepts that the Imams are included among the nonprophetic guided and chosen.
rows.anchor: وروي عن علي بن الحسين عليه السلام أنه قال نحن عنينا بها

rows.speaker: بعض الإمامية
rows.claim: Rūḥ al-Maʿānī reports an Imami narration from ʿAli ibn al-Husayn saying the Imams are intended; its author calls this far from the apparent meaning and disparages Imami reports.
rows.anchor: وروى بعض الإمامية عن علي بن الحسين رضي الله عنهما أنه قال نحن عنينا بهؤلاء القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabaʾi rejects the criticism as mistaken: it assumes the blessed are only prophets by misreading the coordination and making min explanatory, despite Mary’s inclusion among nonprophets.
rows.anchor: وقد تبين خطؤه مما تقدم

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri reports the Prophet predicting that sixty years after the righteous generation a successor group would neglect prayer and follow desires; another would recite Qur’an without it passing their throats, and reciters would include believer, hypocrite, and immoral person.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وتلا هذه الآية

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A report attributed to Abu ʿAbd Allah says they wasted prayer by delaying it beyond its proper times without abandoning it altogether; al-Tabatabaʾi notes similar reports from Ibn Masʿud and several Successors.
rows.anchor: وهو المروي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A report attributed to ʿAli describes following desires as building conspicuously high structures, riding what attracts attention, and wearing famous clothing.
rows.anchor: عن علي عليه السلام من بنى الشديد وركب المنظور ولبس المشهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author quotes a report calling ghayy a valley in Hell, then notes other reports call ghayy and atham rivers there and reads such reports as describing the outcome of error.
rows.anchor: " الغي واد في جهنم " أقول وفي روايات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports that ghayy and atham are rivers in Hell, if authentic, describe the punishment that error leads to; they do not offer a different lexical interpretation, as with reports calling wail a pit and Tuba a tree.
rows.anchor: وهذا على تقدير صحة الحديث ليس بتفسير آخر كما زعمه أكثر المفسرين بل بيان لما سيؤول إليه الغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These two verses interrupt the surrounding passage, yet their Qur’anic style indicates that they are Gabriel’s speech revealed by God; this supports reports that the Prophet asked why Gabriel’s coming was delayed and received this reply by revelation.
rows.anchor: سياقهما يشهد بأنهما من كلام ملك الوحي بوحي قرآني من الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Reports, including one attributed to Ibn ʿAbbas in al-Majmaʿ, say the Prophet found Gabriel’s revelation delayed and asked him about it.
rows.anchor: ورواه في مجمع البيان أيضا عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم استبطأ نزول جبريل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: The author rejects proposed links that insert an implied statement by Gabriel, connect the verses to Gabriel’s earlier words to Mary, or put them in the mouths of the pious in Paradise; context and eloquence disfavor them.
rows.anchor: وهي جميعا وجوه ظاهرة السخافة يأباها السياق ولا يقبلها النظم البليغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanazzul means descending gradually; negation with exception restricts the angels’ descent to God’s command, in line with their never disobeying what He orders.
rows.anchor: والنفي والاستثناء يفيدان الحصر فلا يتنزل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation takes what is before the angels as the future, what is behind as the past, and what lies between as the present.
rows.anchor: فقيل المراد بما بين أيدينا ما هو قدامنا من الزمان المستقبل وبما خلفنا الماضي وبما بين ذلك الحال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes what is before them the time before creation, what is behind them the period after death until the hereafter, and what is between their lifetime.
rows.anchor: ما خلفنا ما بعد الموت إلى استمرار الآخرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view divides time by the two trumpet blasts: before the first, after the second, and between them the forty years separating the blasts.
rows.anchor: الدنيا إلى النفخة الأولى وما خلفهم هو ما بعد النفخه الثانية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view reverses the order, taking what is before them as the hereafter and what is behind them as this world.
rows.anchor: وقيل ما بين أيديهم الآخرة وما خلفهم الدنيا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view means pre-creation, post-annihilation, and the interval between worldly life and the hereafter.
rows.anchor: وقيل ما بين أيديهم ما قبل الخلق وما خلفهم ما بعد الفناء وما بين ذلك ما بين الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation divides the world’s remaining time, its elapsed time, and the present period among the three phrases.
rows.anchor: وقيل ما بين أيديهم ما بقي من أمر الدنيا وما خلفهم ما مضى منه وما بين ذلك ما هم فيه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view refers to the beginning of creation, the ends of their lifespans, and the duration of their lives.
rows.anchor: ابتداء خلقنا ومنتهى آجالنا و مدة حياتنا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One spatial interpretation places heaven ahead, earth behind, and the space between them in the middle phrase.
rows.anchor: وقيل ما بين أيديهم السماء وما خلفهم الأرض وما بين ذلك ما بينهما

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another spatial interpretation reverses heaven and earth’s positions in the first two phrases.
rows.anchor: وقيل بعكس ذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another spatial reading means the place to which angels move, the place from which they move, and the place where they are.
rows.anchor: وقيل ما بين أيديهم المكان الذي ينتقلون إليه وما خلفهم المكان الذي ينتقلون منه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view says the wording covers both time and place.
rows.anchor: وهناك قول بكون الآية تعم الزمان والمكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author counts eleven interpretations but finds no evidence for them and objects that they measure angels by human categories; he instead reads the phrases as angels’ effects, their prior causes, and their own existence, encompassing them completely.
rows.anchor: فهذه أحد عشر قولا ولا دليل على شيء منها مع ما فيها من قياس الملك على الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s ownership explains why angels descend only by command: their existence, antecedents, and effects all belong to Him, and they neither disobey nor will except with His permission.
rows.anchor: يفيد إحاطة ملكه تعالى بهم ملكا حقيقيا لا يجري فيه تصرف غيره ولا إرادة من سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s comprehensive ownership explains the command restriction, while not being forgetful completes that rationale: nothing in His domain is neglected in His governance.
rows.anchor: من تمام التعليل أي إنه تعالى لا ينسى شيئا من ملكه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported reading says God did not forget or abandon His prophets; although it can fit one occasion report, it leaves the ownership phrase without its explanatory role and disconnects the next verse.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى وما كان ربك نسيا أي تاركا لأنبيائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God Lord of the heavens, earth, and all between them explains His ownership and unfailing governance, since lordship entails ownership and managing affairs.
rows.anchor: تعليل لقوله في الآية السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to worship and persevere follows because the message is God’s own call: worship Him alone, since there is no other lord to replace Him or share worship.
rows.anchor: فالكلام كلامه والدعوة دعوته فاعبده وحده واصطبر لعبادته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The author rejects making worship and perseverance follow directly from the phrase Lord of the heavens or from God not being forgetful; those links do not fit the argument.
rows.anchor: وربما قيل إن الجملة تفريع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about a namesake completes the rationale for worship: no one shares the name Lord and its universal, absolute lordship so as to merit worship instead.
rows.anchor: من تمام البيان المقصود بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samiyy means one sharing the name Lord, because the argument establishes God’s absolute lordship over everything.
rows.anchor: المراد بالسمي المشارك في الاسم والمراد بالاسم هو الرب لأن مقتضى بيان الآية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The author rejects glosses of samiyy as a figurative equal, a child, or as a shared proper name meaning God, Allah, deity, al-Rahman, or the creator and giver of life and death.
rows.anchor: فقد قيل إن المراد بالسمي المماثل مجازا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeatedly addressing the angels’ speaker as your Lord prepares the declaration of oneness: the angels’ Lord is the Prophet’s Lord, so the call to worship is His; the surah’s opening has the same coherent aim.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أن ربنا الذي نتنزل عن أمره هو ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship and perseverance express unity of worship; remaining constant in worship is implied by, rather than a separate sense beyond, the command to worship.
rows.anchor: مسوق لتوحيد العبادة وليس أمرا بالعبادة وأمرا بالثبات عليها وإدامتها إلا من جهة الملازمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed continuation makes the two verses confirm the preceding revelation: Gabriel was commanded to deliver the surah and then clarify that he descended only by God’s command, whose call is to worship the sole Lord.
rows.anchor: فكأن ملك الوحي لما تنزل عليه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بالسورة وأوحى إليه الآيات الثلاث والستين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king-and-messenger analogy shows how Gabriel’s explanatory words remain a message from God; this reading fits the verses better and more clearly than varying, weak occasion reports.
rows.anchor: وهذا نظير أن يرسل ملك رسولا بكتاب من عنده أو رسالة إلى بعض عماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage returns to the thread before the angelic interlude and appends examples of the corrupt successors’ error; across seven verses it addresses denial of resurrection and its consequences, alongside claims about prophethood and creation.
rows.anchor: عود إلى ما قبل قوله

rows.speaker: الكافر
rows.claim: The statement voices the denial of resurrection found among idolaters and others who deny a creator, and can reflect the unreasoned inclination of human nature before considering proof.
rows.anchor: وإنما عبر بالإنسان لكونه لا يترقب منه ذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported explanation says the speaker is called human because this denial is an unexpected thing for a human being; the author says it does not fit the following oath to resurrect and punish them.
rows.anchor: قيل ولذلك نسب القول إلى الإنسان حينما كان مقتضى طبع الكلام أن يقال ويقول الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker is likely an unbeliever denying resurrection; calling him human stresses that reason should prevent him from finding a second creation implausible when he remembers God first created him from nothing.
rows.anchor: وليس ببعيد أن يكون المراد بالإنسان القائل ذلك هو الكافر المنكر للبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense signals that denial of resurrection continues among deniers and doubters.
rows.anchor: للإشارة إلى استمرار هذا الاستبعاد بين المنكرين للمعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question answers doubt by citing an earlier comparable creation, establishing the possibility of resurrection, like the argument from first creation in the linked passage.
rows.anchor: قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An objection says that creating something similar proves only possibility, whereas resurrection requires the same individual, not merely a likeness.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل الاحتجاج بوقوع المثل إنما ينتج إمكان المثل والمطلوب في إثبات المعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person’s identity depends on the enduring individual soul, not an unchanged body; recreating a body and reconnecting that soul restores the same person, as personal identity persists despite bodily change in life.
rows.anchor: وشخصية الشخص الإنساني بنفسه لا ببدنه فإذا خلق البدن ثانيا وتعلقت به النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The related passage says people are taken from their bodies at death yet preserved, so they are not lost from God’s knowledge or power.
rows.anchor: أي إنكم مأخوذون من أبدانكم محفوظون لا تضلون ولا تفتقدون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The root sense of jithiyyan is a plural of kneeling person; Ibn ʿAbbas reportedly takes it as heaps of earth or stones, which the author finds more apt to the gathering context.
rows.anchor: ونسب إلى ابن عباس أنه جمع جثوة وهو المجتمع من التراب والحجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns for gathering and bringing refer to unbelievers, who are assembled outside their graves with their satanic allies or companions.
rows.anchor: للكفار، والآية إلى تمام ثلاث آيات متعرضة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The author rejects taking both pronouns to include all people, believers and unbelievers, because the passage’s tone of wrath and punishment rules that out.
rows.anchor: وربما قيل إن الضميرين للناس أعم من المؤمن والكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers may be gathered with satanic allies because they followed error, or with their personal satanic companions, as another cited passage describes.
rows.anchor: أو المراد حشرهم مع قرنائهم من الشياطين كما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath means they will be gathered with their allies or companions and brought around Hell in humiliation, either individually kneeling or in packed groups.
rows.anchor: والمعنى فاقسم بربك لنجمعنهم - يوم القيامة -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form shifts from first-person plural to third person in by your Lord, perhaps echoing the phrase your Lord in the angelic reply and the later assertion of God’s decree.
rows.anchor: من التكلم مع الغير إلى الغيبة ولعل النكتة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root n-z-ʿ means extract; a shiʿa is a cooperating group or followers of a shared belief; ʿitiyy is a verbal noun for rebellious defiance.
rows.anchor: والشيعة الجماعة المتعاونون على أمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative who is most rebellious functions as the object of extract, highlighting careful selection; the singled-out people are the factional leaders and guides of error.
rows.anchor: جملة استفهامية وضع موضع مفعول لننزعن للدلالة على العناية بالتعيين والتمييز

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation extracts the most rebellious first, then the next most rebellious, continuing until all have been singled out.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى لنستخرجن الأشد ثم الأشد حتى يحاط بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase against the Merciful signals the exceptional gravity of their defiance: His mercy encompasses everything, and they experienced only mercy from Him.
rows.anchor: تلويح أن تمردهم عظيم لكونه تمردا على من شملت رحمته كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣilyan is the verbal noun of enduring the fire’s heat; God knows best who deserves to suffer it and the different degrees of their deserts.
rows.anchor: الصلي في الأصل على فعول مصدر يقال صلي النار يصلاها صليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address includes all people, believers and unbelievers, as the next verse distinguishes the pious from wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: الخطاب للناس عامة مؤمنيهم وكافريهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The alternative restricts the address to the unbelievers just discussed and reads the shift as rhetorical; the author says the following verse’s contrast rules this out.
rows.anchor: وربما قيل إن الخطاب للكفار المذكورين في الآيات الثلاث الماضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wurud originally means aiming for or approaching water, contrasted with departing; it is also used figuratively or emphatically for approaching Hell, so the word itself need not mean entering it.
rows.anchor: الورود خلاف الصدور وهو قصد الماء على ما يظهر من كتب اللغة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes say people only approach and overlook the Fire rather than enter it, citing the usage of coming to Midian’s water, a water drawer, and the righteous being kept away from Hell’s sound.
rows.anchor: ولما ورد ماء مدين وجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those examples of approaching water do not rule out literal entry elsewhere; believers’ distance from Hell may follow their entry, or God may screen them from its sound, as He cooled the fire for Abraham.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن استعماله في مثل قوله

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Many exegetes infer entry into Hell from passages saying the worshippers and what they worship are its fuel and Pharaoh led his people into it.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون ولعلهم أكثر المفسرين بدلالة الآية على دخولهم النار استنادا إلى مثل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: They also argue that leaving the wrongdoers there implies they were already inside, and cite reports interpreting the event as entry.
rows.anchor: ويدل عليه قوله في الآية التالية

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Among those who infer entry, some include everyone, while others restrict entry to the non-pious and read from among you as from among them, citing the Paradise reward passage.
rows.anchor: وهؤلاء بين من يقول بدخول عامة الناس فيها ومن يقول بدخول غير المتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says restricting the verse to unbelievers or non-pious people does not fit the next verse’s contrast between pious people and wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: هذا ولكن لا يلائمه سياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited passages about worshippers being brought to Hell and Pharaoh leading his people can mean arrival or leading toward it, not entry; Pharaoh guides his people to Hell but does not himself insert them.
rows.anchor: فإن شأن فرعون وهو من أئمة الضلال هو أن يهدي قومه إلى النار وأما إدخالهم فيها فليس إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaving wrongdoers there indicates that they are inside, but does not prove that wurud itself means entry; rescue can also mean keeping the pious away from imminent danger.
rows.anchor: فالآية دالة على كونهم داخلين فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interpreting wurud as merely a person’s innate potential to enter fails because the verse calls the event a decree God has imposed, not an inclination arising from human nature.
rows.anchor: فإنه صريح في أن هذا الورود بإيراد من الله وبقضائه المحتوم لا باقتضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wurud denotes no more than purposeful arrival and approach; the next verse may still show that all or only wrongdoers enter after arriving.
rows.anchor: والحق أن الورود لا يدل على أزيد من الحضور والإشراف عن قصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in was decreed refers either to the approach itself or to the preceding ruling; the phrase means it is decisively decreed by God, who alone may impose such a decree.
rows.anchor: أي هذا الورود أو الحكم كان واجبا عليه تعالى مقضيا في حقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaving the wrongdoers in the Fire indicates their entry; rescuing the pious does not prove they entered, although pairing the two verbs may suggest it, and their wrongdoing explains their fate.
rows.anchor: وفي التعبير بلفظ الظالمين إشارة إلى علية الوصف للحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both pious and wrongdoers approach the Fire under a binding divine decree; God then rescues the pious and leaves the wrongdoers kneeling in it for their injustice.
rows.anchor: ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا منها ونترك الظالمين فيها

rows.speaker: مالك الجهني
rows.claim: A report from Malik al-Juhani quoting Abu ʿAbd Allah explains that before creation the human was neither determined nor written down.
rows.anchor: عن مالك الجهني قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن قول الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: حمران
rows.claim: A report from Ḥumran quoting Abu ʿAbd Allah says the human was not in a book or knowledge before creation.
rows.anchor: عن حمران قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These reports mean the person was absent from the changeable records until God willed creation, not from the Preserved Tablet, which according to the Qur’an contains everything.
rows.anchor: المراد بالحديثين أنه لم يكن في كتاب ولا علم من كتب المحو والإثبات

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi explains jithiyyan as being on their knees.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: الحسين بن أبي العلاء
rows.claim: A report from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-ʿAlaʾ quoting Abu ʿAbd Allah says wurud is like saying we came to a people, without entering their place.
rows.anchor: وفيه بإسناده عن الحسين بن أبي العلاء عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Murra al-Hamdani related Ibn Masʿud’s report from the Prophet: people reach the Fire and leave according to their deeds, moving at speeds from lightning and wind to a walk.
rows.anchor: عن السدي قال سألت مرة الهمداني عن هذه الآية فحدثني أن عبد الله بن مسعود حدثهم عن رسول الله

rows.speaker: أبو سمية
rows.claim: Abu Sumayya reports disagreement over whether believers enter the Fire; he asked Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, who swore that he heard the Prophet’s answer continued in the next segment.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سمية قال أختلفنا في الورود فقال قوم لا يدخلها مؤمن وقال آخرون يدخلونها جميعا

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah reports the Prophet saying that everyone, righteous and wicked, enters the Fire; for believers it becomes cool and safe like Abraham’s fire, then God rescues the pious and leaves wrongdoers kneeling. Al-Tabatabaʾi grades its chain weak because of an unknown narrator.
rows.anchor: الورود الدخول لا يبقى بر ولا فاجر حتى يدخلها فتكون على المؤمنين بردا وسلاما

rows.speaker: يعلى بن منبه
rows.claim: A report raised from Yaʿla ibn Munabbih to the Prophet says the Fire tells a believer to pass because his light has extinguished its flames.
rows.anchor: وروي مرفوعا عن يعلى بن منبه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Another report from the Prophet says God makes the Fire solid like ghee, gathers creation, and commands it to take its own people and leave His friends; it recognizes them better than a mother recognizes her child.
rows.anchor: إن الله يجعل النار كالسمن الجامد ويجمع عليها الخلق ثم ينادي المنادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthur collected the last four reports from several books; its copy used by the author omits the wording that wurud means entry in the second report.
rows.anchor: والروايات الأربع الأخيرة رواها في الدر المنثور عن عدة من أرباب الكتب والجوامع

rows.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
rows.claim: ʿUrwa reports that Ibn Rawaha wept while departing for Muʾta, not from worldly attachment, but because the Prophet recited the verse and Ibn Rawaha knew he would enter the Fire and did not know how he would emerge.
rows.anchor: عن عروة بن الزبير قال لما أراد ابن رواحة الخروج إلى أرض مؤتة من الشام أتاه المسلمون

rows.speaker: الصدوق
rows.claim: Some reports imply that people cross over the Fire on the bridge of the ṣirāṭ; the righteous cross it and the wicked fall, and al-Ṣaduq applies the verse to this account.
rows.anchor: ظاهر بعض الروايات السابقة أن ورود الناس النار هو جوازهم منها فينطبق على روايات الصراط

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ offers another rationale: showing believers Hell magnifies their gratitude for Paradise, while showing wrongdoers the Paradise they lost deepens their regret.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن الفائدة في ذلك يعني ورود النار ما روي في بعض الأخبار أن الله تعالى لا يدخل أحدا الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has unrestricted, absolute ownership of all things and can dispose of them without blame; blame applies when an agent acts outside what it owns under a human law, whose ownership is necessarily limited by social life.
rows.anchor: له تعالى الملك المطلق على الأشياء بمعنى أنه يملك كل شيء ملكا مطلقا غير مقيد بحال أو زمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The analogy of a human master abusing a slave cannot limit divine ownership because human ownership differs categorically from God’s unrestricted ownership.
rows.anchor: والاستدلال على محدودية ملكه تعالى بما وراء القبائح العقلية بأنا نرى أن المالك لعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s legislative ownership rests on ontological ownership: all things exist through Him, so no thing can have real existence without His creative sovereignty; sin is only disobedience and neglected wisdom, not an independently created object.
rows.anchor: كون كل شيء بحيث يقوم وجوده به تعالى وهذا هو الملك التكويني الذي لا يخلو شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No other being can impose a legal duty or prohibition on God, just as none can affect Him causally; that would make Him subject to another’s ownership, and reason’s judgements themselves depend on interests beyond reason.
rows.anchor: لا معنى لأن يوجب غيره تعالى عليه شيئا أو يحرم أو يجوز وبالجملة يكلفه بتكليف تشريعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a real interest exists outside God, it is a created effect of His and the supposed obligation returns to His own act; if it is merely conceptual, reason would be judging itself without an external basis.
rows.anchor: وإما أمر حقيقي موجود في الخارج ولا محالة هي ممكنة معلولة للواجب ينتهي وجوده إليه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s absolute ownership means He may do what He wills and no one can revise His decree, as the cited verses affirm.
rows.anchor: أن له ملكا مطلقا لا يتقيد بتصرف دون تصرف فله أن يفعل ما يشاء ويحكم ما يريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the level of guidance and legislation God obligates Himself to some norms and bars Himself from others, approving justice and beneficence and rejecting injustice as He does for people.
rows.anchor: غير أنه تعالى بما كلمنا في مرحلة الهداية على قدر عقولنا ونصب نفسه في مقام التشريع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The created order guides human powers and circumstances toward interests that secure worldly and otherworldly happiness; innate disposition and revelation announce the corresponding way of life as divine law.
rows.anchor: قدر وجودنا في نظام متقن يربطه إلى غايات هي سعادتنا وفيها خير دنيانا وآخرتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God is lawgiver, its commands and prohibitions are His; justice is always good and approved by Him, while injustice is condemned and never approved for His acts or ours.
rows.anchor: وهذه القوانين التي تهتف بها الفطرة ويعلمها الوحي السماوي هي الشريعة وإذ هي تنتهي إليه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no contradiction in saying an act is legislatively obligatory on God when He legislates for Himself; such rational judgements are conventional labels for His established practice, not external powers over Him.
rows.anchor: فلا ضير في وجوب شيء عليه تعالى وجوبا تشريعيا إذا كان هو المشرع على نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Legislative obligation differs from causal necessity, which is grounded in the necessary order of causes and effects and underlies the rational attribution of justice.
rows.anchor: هذا الوجوب تشريعي وهناك وجوب آخر تكويني يعتمد عليه هذا الوجوب

rows.speaker: بعض الباحثين
rows.claim: Some researchers mistake the duty for a causal necessity: although God can do wrong, they say divine wisdom makes abstaining from it metaphysically necessary; the author calls this reasoning fallacious.
rows.anchor: وقد التبس الأمر على كثير من الباحثين فزعموا كون هذا الوجوب تكوينيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the divine essence is the complete cause, the act is necessary with or without an added wisdom; if the essence is only part of the cause, the act is possible relative to it and necessary only with the full cause.
rows.anchor: المغالطة إنما نشأت من أخذ الفعل ضروريا بالنسبة إلى الذات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling an act obligatory or forbidden for God is a judgement made by practical reason, not the discovery of an independently existing rule; its normative concepts exist in rational consideration.
rows.anchor: والعقل في ذلك حاكم قاض لا مدرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Practical reason judges what ought or ought not be done, while theoretical reason receives and describes real, nonconventional meanings that exist independently of its act of knowing.
rows.anchor: وأما العقل النظري الذي موطن عمله المعاني الحقيقية غير الاعتبارية تصورا أو تصديقا
